summary: Round 3, every claim below measured by mutation in an issued tree on these exact staged bytes (28ac146). Pristine :sequencer:test = 383 green before and after every mutation; each mutation was reverted with `git checkout --` and the suite re-run. FOUR OF ROUND 2'S FIVE MINORS ARE FIXED AND EACH FIX IS PINNED BY THE MUTATION IT WAS WRITTEN FOR. (1) `landed.sequence() > 0` -> `> 1` now reddens exactly ONE test, LocalSequencerSealRaceTest#aCrossedEpochThatOnlyOPENEDIsStillTheAncestor: 383 completed, 1 failed. The open-only interleave is the minimal one and lands the seal at slot 1, which is the only value separating the two predicates. (2) BOTH forcings of the origin flag are now dead. `boolean atOrigin = originIsOwnChain` -> `true` reddens ChainReplayEmptyOriginTest#inheritedCROSSESAnEmptyOriginToReachTheOffsets; -> `false` reddens #replayDoesNOTCrossItsOWNEmptyChain with `Expecting empty but was: {RunKey[...aa, partitionId=0]=3L}`. ASKED SPECIFICALLY WHETHER replayDoesNOTCrossItsOWNEmptyChain IS VACUOUS: IT IS NOT -- it is the only test in the module that kills the `false` forcing, and it is the reason the flag can stay a parameter rather than becoming a constant. (3) `recoverChainEnd()` deletion is dead: commenting out `burned.recoverChainEnd();` reddens exactly aRacingChainLONGERThanTheRedriveBudgetStillConverges with `java.io.IOException: seal did not converge at seq 8 within 8 redrive(s)`, which is the outage the production reviewer measured, not a request-count nicety. (4) ASKED WHETHER THE FAULTED SWEEP EARNS ITS RUNTIME: yes on cost, and it is NOT vacuous, but I could not find a mutant it uniquely kills. It runs in 0.645s of a 6s module suite. Reverting both production files to their pre-image reddens it with `seed 0: I2 -- stream RunKey[...] resumes at 106 but the chain had assigned up to 111`, so the fault profile does fire and the checkers do work on it. Both arms stand alone: deleting the ambiguousPut assertion and re-running under the revert still reddens on `and under the mixed profile too` at seed 55. But every mutation it killed was also killed by a sub-second unit test -- full revert: sweep + 5 unit tests; firstInheritableAncestor `atOrigin = false` -> `true`: sweep + 2 unit tests. Four further mutations (loop start `epoch - 1` -> `epoch - 2`; `break` after the first crossed epoch; dropping `prevEpoch = crossed`; `landed.sequence() > 1`) were killed by unit tests and NOT by the sweep. So its value is rule-20 coverage of shapes the five hand-built fixtures do not construct, not a measured unique kill; at 0.645s that is worth having and I am not filing it. (5) THE CLASS SPLIT STRANDED AND WEAKENED NOTHING. Constants match across the seam (both files: PREFIX = "bins/cluster-a", STREAM = ...0000aa), and a divergence would fail loudly on a missing key rather than pass vacuously. The moved test is verbatim -- diffing the removed lines against the new file leaves only the three visibility changes plus assertions removed in ALREADY-REVIEWED rounds, and those were replaced by their STRONGER opposites, `isEqualTo(new Seal(0, 4))` on each burned epoch, which is the ADR-0037 inversion rather than a loosening. Round-1 blocking finding M4.47-R1a stays fixed and is pinned three ways: dropping `prevEpoch = crossed;` reddens all three LocalSequencerSealRaceTest cases. INDEPENDENTLY ON check-mutants, which the packet shows FAILED: I ran PIT myself scoped to the two changed classes in my own isolated tree -- 119 mutants, 109 killed, 92%, above the 80% floor -- so the packet's failure is M0.88's shared-report corruption, not a real score. The only SURVIVED mutant inside M4.47's own hunks is `firstInheritableAncestor` L373 `replaced long return with 0`, which is already filed as M4.48; every other survivor is in untouched code (close, renewForever logging).

findings.finding: CARRIED, NOW FILED AS BACKLOG ROW M4.49 rather than fixed, which is the right disposition for a minor. Not re-measured by me this round; round 2's measurement stands: `closing.continuedAt() > epoch` -> `> Long.MAX_VALUE` and -> `!= epoch` both leave the suite green, and the gap loop's start reverted to `closing.continuedAt()` also survives. Only the loop's EXISTENCE is pinned. Recorded here so the row and the measurement stay attached to each other.
findings.failure_scenario: The LATER-epoch arm of checkLink is deleted or inverted and nothing goes red: the checker stops reporting a chain that continues from an ancestor sealed for an epoch ABOVE it, which is the fork case, and the sweep that would otherwise catch it is the only instrument that can see it.
findings.suggested: M4.49: one fixture whose ancestor Seal names a HIGHER epoch than the chain under test.

findings.finding: RE-MEASURED THIS ROUND BY PIT IN MY OWN TREE, and already filed as backlog row M4.48. `return chainEpoch` -> `return 0` is the one SURVIVED mutant inside M4.47's changed hunks (PIT: 119 mutants, 109 killed, 92%). The seal loop above it converges on the same epoch and sets the same prevEpoch/prevSeq pair, so the walk's return value changes nothing observable -- which makes this a design finding about the walk being subsumed, not a missing assertion.
findings.failure_scenario: The walk's return value is edited -- an off-by-one, or a wrong Math.max floor -- and no test goes red, because the loop below independently arrives at the same answer. The defect only surfaces if the loop is later simplified in a way that starts trusting the walk again.
findings.suggested: M4.48 as filed: delete the walk, or pin its return value directly.
